60111.name: Professionele Vaardigheden 2
60111.entryRequirements: Bachelor Pedagogische Wetenschappen studenten: behaald Professionele Vaardigheden 1. Minorstudenten: zie aanbevolen voorkennis.
60111.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Het behalen van Professionele Vaardigheden-I is voor de bachelorstudenten Pedagogische Wetenschappen een ingangseis voor het vak Professionele Vaardigheden - II in bachelorjaar 2. Studenten die het vak Professionele Vaardigheden II in het kader van de minorprogramma's "Preventieve Jeugdhulp en opvoeding", "Orthopedagogiek" of "Orthopedagogiek Uitgebreid" willen volgen, wordt geadviseerd basiskennis communicatievaardigheden te hebben. Echter is dit voor deze groep studenten geen ingangseis. Als blijkt dat uit de vignetten-toets (eerste bijeenkomst) onvoldoende kennis aanwezig is, dan moet een extra opdracht gemaakt worden. Het vak Professionele Vaardigheden II is onderdeel van het orthopedagogiektraject dat (wanneer het reguliere bachelorprorgramma wordt gevolgd), inclusief de masteropleiding Orthopedagogiek, toelating geeft tot de NVO-registraties voor orthopedagogen en de postdoctorale of post-master opleiding tot GZ-psycholoog en Schoolpsycholoog.

components: Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 1
Introduction to Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 2
Academic Skills A and B are compulsory in year 1. They carry no separate EC: their workload is credited within the content courses.

The normal programme requires a 6 EC internship, including approved practice or research experience, preparation, reflection and supervision. The course entry also offers a 9 EC variant; this example uses the prescribed 6 EC component. Students arrange an approved host and complete the required information and application training before starting.
Policy and Organisation of Childrearing and Education

Year 2 requires at least 42 first-year EC. Academic Skills C and D are compulsory with no separate EC. Testing and Measurement follows participation in Descriptive Statistics; Inferential Statistics requires passing Descriptive Statistics; Research in Practice requires passing both Descriptive Statistics and Testing and Measurement. Professional Skills 2 requires passing Professional Skills 1.
Empirical Bachelor Thesis in Pedagogical Sciences

The 15 EC empirical thesis follows completion of the first two years, except that one year-2 content course and Academic Skills D may remain. At least nine colloquium points are also required for graduation: five from POW master-thesis presentations, one from a doctorate or inaugural lecture, and three from POW or Comenius lectures or conferences.

Professional Skills 3 requires passing Professional Skills 2 and following Diagnostics. Following means a recorded assessment result. It develops practical child and adolescent assessment and advice skills.

The 30 EC open space remains unspecified. Choices must not overlap the compulsory curriculum. Second- and third-year faculty courses can be selected without extra approval. First-year courses normally need to form part of a completed minor; other choices, skills and language courses require prior Examination Board approval. Exchange also requires approval.
findings: The 2026–2027 dated normal curriculum and OER B4.2 pp. 21–22 agree on twenty-seven credited components. The two introductions are combined Pedagogical and Educational Sciences 1 and 2, not separate single-discipline introductions. Year two includes Developmental Psychopathology, not an undifferentiated psychopathology course. Academic Skills A–D are compulsory and their workload is included within credited courses rather than added to the 180 EC.

OER B5.6 pp. 30–31 requires forty-two first-year EC before year-two study. Testing and Measurement requires a recorded participation result in Descriptive Statistics. Inferential Statistics requires passing Descriptive Statistics; Research in Practice requires passing Descriptive Statistics and Testing and Measurement. Professional Skills 2 requires Professional Skills 1; Professional Skills 3 requires passing Skills 2 and following Diagnostics. Skills C and D require passing A or B. The illustrated full progression completes the preceding years and all these conditions.

The empirical thesis entry and OER B5.6 allow one year-two content course and Academic Skills D to remain, with all other first- and second-year work completed. Its fifteen EC cover a supervised empirical investigation, an individual question within a lecturer-led topic and an empirical article. OER B5.14 p. 33 requires nine colloquium points, specifically five POW master-thesis presentations, one doctorate or inaugural lecture and three POW/Comenius lectures or conferences. These are separate non-credit graduation obligations.

Bachelor Internship 70120270AY is six EC in the degree table. Its course entry permits a nine-EC variant, which is not stacked onto this pathway. The six-EC version is 168 hours including 126 practice hours. Students arrange an approved practice/research host, register and complete the required information and application training before starting. The current offering lists preparation in April or October, September/February practice patterns, time registration, reflection and intervision. A February year-two start follows earlier preparation; no future deadline is invented. OER B5.6 supplies the year-two entry rule and no additional internship-specific passed-course condition.

OER B4.4–B4.5 pp. 23–24 controls the unspecified thirty-EC open space: no overlap, year-two/three faculty courses without extra approval, first-year courses only within a minor, other choices and skills/language courses needing approval. The guide choice page says language-skills courses are excluded, while the adopted OER requires approval. The adopted regulation controls; no language or skills choice is instantiated and the reader-facing note states the approval requirement. A completed UvA minor may fill the space subject to non-overlap; outside choices and exchange need approval. This bounded discrepancy does not affect the unfilled thirty-EC allowance.

The remaining course entries establish the dedicated family, peer, learning, personality, educator-quality and practice sequence. Qualitative research covers narrative, focus groups, oral history, observation and case studies. Research in Practice focuses on single-case designs, change assessment, data management and ethical inquiry. The diagnostic and professional-skills modules are child- and context-focused. All remain represented without inventing a minor or professional qualification.
